title: Federated shared/private Mirror residual frontier
hypothesis: Across increasing client heterogeneity, one shared global weight basis plus one client phase and rank-1 private residuals for outlier clients will preserve client function quality while reducing actual storage/communication versus a FedRep-style full private residual. The phase mechanism must be compared with direct coefficients and native scalar-phase control. The sweep will locate when private state dominates.
physical_object: one shared 16x16 global client model with two shared functional update directions
mirror_coordinate: one phase angle per client selecting a shared common update
logical_multiplicity: 64 client functions across five nested heterogeneity rates (0, 25, 50, 75, 100 percent outliers)
controls: shared phase with no private residual
shared phase plus rank-1 private residuals
direct two-coefficient basis plus the same private residuals
native scalar-phase implementation identical to Mirror
FedRep-style shared basis plus dense private residual matrices

development.selection_metric: overall/aligned/outlier nMSE, actual serialized total bytes, private residual bytes, client communication by heterogeneity, MAC proxy

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY FP32 inference payload bytes after reload
paid_objects: private rank-1 factors or dense matrices

success_gate: At fresh heterogeneity rates 25% and 50%: private-enabled Mirror nMSE <=1e-5 for aligned and outlier cohorts and actual payload <=0.80x FedRep-style dense-private payload. Report full 0–100% sweep and private-byte/communication slope. No Mirror-specific claim unless at least 10% below direct/native controls.
failure_gate: At either primary fresh rate (25% or 50%), private-enabled Mirror misses quality or saves <20% versus FedRep dense-private state in at least two fresh worlds; or private-state cost eliminates the shared-state advantage across all rates. Native/direct equivalence only blocks Mirror-specific attribution, not the shared/private frontier comparison.
development_decision: Both development worlds passed quality and the 20% FedRep payload margin at heterogeneity 25% and 50%, but not at 0%. Before fresh access, define 25% and 50% as the primary operating region and retain the entire sweep as secondary. Mirror/native phase state was identical, so the result can only support a shared/private application frontier, not a Mirror-specific gain.
amendment: Following development-only inspection, freeze primary heterogeneity rates to 25% and 50% because the zero-outlier endpoint did not meet the registered Pareto margin. Fresh seeds 34611–34613 are unchanged; no model or byte threshold changed. All five heterogeneity rates will still be reported.
boundaries: synthetic post-fit client linear functions, not trained federated models
outlier IDs and phase codes are oracle-known; no client-side learning or adaptation
private residuals are planted rank-1 factors; the dense FedRep control is intentionally stronger in private expressivity
sweeping outlier fraction is a storage/quality frontier, not a capacity claim
